entries.core_move: Apply the sifting property to convert an integral of a continuous-time signal multiplied by a shifted unit impulse into the signal value sampled at the impulse location.
Evaluate integrals containing shifted unit impulses by checking whether the impulse time lies inside the integration limits and substituting the sampled value when it does.
Rewrite impulses with nonstandard arguments as scaled shifted impulses by locating each argument zero and applying the correct inverse-slope weight.
Apply change-of-variables reasoning to evaluate impulse integrals by transforming the impulse argument, adjusting the scale factor, and preserving the correct sampled time.

entries.lesson_title: Unit Step as the Integral of an Impulse
entries.core_move: Convert the accumulated integral of a shifted unit impulse into a shifted unit step by identifying when the impulse area has been included.

entries.lesson_title: Unit Impulse as the Derivative of a Unit Step
entries.core_move: Differentiate a shifted unit step to convert its instantaneous jump into the corresponding shifted unit impulse.
